description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Joern fixture that carries six findings whose bytecode coordinate is absent rather than unresolvable -- the class member missing, null, empty, whitespace-only, or carrying the collector's '<unknown>' sentinel. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, and every path was resolved from the documented indexing scheme before the adapter was run; the run came afterwards, to corroborate. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. The key names are the ones expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json established and expected/joern.rows.json extends -- the shared metadata keys, the three parts rows / row_derivations / rejections, and the negative-only additions routing, rejection_boundary, rejections and counts.parse_status -- so one generic loader reads every expected file in this tree.
scanner_class_authority: AAP 0.5.4's class table fixes sast for opengrep, semgrep, datadog-static-analyzer and joern. The value is fixed in advance rather than derived from what the artifact turns out to contain, and it is identical on every row. Trivy is the single tool whose scanner_class varies by record, and joern is not it.
artifact_shape_note: This is the only artifact whose shape is the harness's own collector output rather than a tool-native format. There is no Joern output format to look up: harness/bin/run-joern.sh loads the code-property graph with importCpg, runs the bounded query set baked into harness/lib/joern-scan.sc, and that script writes the artifact itself.

fixture.shape: the collector shape the specification documents
fixture.derived_from: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/reject-joern-unresolvable-path.json, which is itself derived from harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json
fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from captured output rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation. Three things are derived and nothing else is invented. First, the envelope: tool, cpg_path, generated_at, cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size, declaration_index_size and all five queries[] elements are carried across from the unresolvable-path sibling unchanged, so the two fixtures describe the same graph and the same query set. Second, the three sound records: findings 0, 7 and 8 here are that sibling's findings 0, 1 and 3, carried across member for member, so the well-formed neighbours this fixture emits are already-verified records rather than newly authored ones. Third, the six defective records: each is that sibling's shape with its class coordinate removed or emptied in one of six distinct ways, its path member set to null, and a method signature, a message and a line supplied for the call site it names. That sibling's findings[2] -- the shaded MessageDigestHashFunction record -- is deliberately excluded, because its coordinate is present and resolves to nothing, which is the opposite condition and the sibling's own subject.
fixture.why_six_defective_records: absent_path is one class reached through six materially different artifact shapes and two different code paths, and a fixture carrying one of them would leave the other five uncovered while the class still appeared covered. The six are enumerated under the_six_defective_shapes with the member state each carries, and the two code paths under the_two_classification_routes. Five share one detail string and one identity spelling; the sixth -- the sentinel -- has its own detail and its own identity key set, which is exactly the distinction a single-record fixture would have hidden.
fixture.why_the_documented_shape_is_the_right_ca: Two reasons. This provisioning's collector shape cannot carry the condition at all in one of its six forms: the '<unknown>' sentinel and the path / path_resolution members are documented-shape members, and the sentinel route is the only route through the adapter's own _with_explanation composition. And the six negative fixtures in this tree are all written in the documented shape, so carrying it here keeps the negative set internally consistent -- the positive fixture joern.json is the one that covers this provisioning's shape, and expected/joern.rows.json says so.
fixture.no_secret_or_absolute_emitted_value: No credential-shaped string occurs in the fixture, and the only absolute path in it is the envelope's cpg_path, which names the graph file, reaches no dataset field and is deliberately not copied into this document.
fixture.excerpt_note: The fixture is never edited to suit these rows; these rows are re-derived when the fixture changes.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- SARIF is a version of "2.1.0" together with a runs array, and this document carries neither, so it is a native artifact routed by the runner that wrote it
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("joern", doc) returns tool "joern", shape "native", adapter "joern", scanner_class "sast"
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No shape-detection failure is expected here, and a test asserting one against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing. The enclosing document is a well-formed native Joern artifact and routes cleanly; six of its nine findings are defective in their coordinate member, and the adapter rejects those six while still emitting the other three. A finding whose coordinate member is missing is not a malformed record: the record is a JSON object with a rule identifier, a message, a method signature and a line, so it passes the shape step and is decided at the path step. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py. A Joern artifact is a native artifact, so it is eligible material for that assertion, but the assertion itself is not this file's and is not made here.
routing.caller_fault_is_not_a_rejection: normalize.adapters.joern.JoernAdapterError describes a defective call -- the wrong tool identifier, a relative root, another tool's path base, a path base whose kind is not bytecode_class, or a document that is not an object -- and stops the caller. None of those is in play here, and none is ever counted as a rejection: a caller fault absorbed into a rejection count would let a wrong root produce a plausible dataset for a whole tool.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant, which harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py restates as its own FIELDS because AAP 0.6.4 permits an adapter to import paths and severity and nothing else. The two were compared and are identical. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS. path in particular is not an optional field (AAP 0.5.4), which is the whole reason each of this fixture's six defective records is a counted rejection rather than a row with a null path. Note the distinction the two absence conventions make here: a finding member may legitimately be absent from an artifact, and a dataset field may not be absent from a row. This fixture is built on exactly that difference.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

shape_divergence.summary: This fixture is written in the collector shape the specification documents, which is the opposite half of the divergence expected/joern.rows.json records: that fixture captures this provisioning's shape. The divergence itself is recorded, not repaired -- AAP 0.1.3's authority rule -- and the adapter reads both shapes in a fixed field precedence so the choice is reproducible. Five members differ from the provisioned shape, and each changes a value below. The class coordinate is the one this fixture turns on: in the provisioned shape it is spelled class and in the documented shape class_file, and the adapter tries them in that order, so a record carrying neither reaches the path step with no coordinate at all.
shape_divergence.documented_shape: {tool, cpg_path, generated_at, cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size, declaration_index_size, queries: [{id, count}], findings: [{rule_id, message, path, start_line, method_full_name, class_file, path_resolution}]}
shape_divergence.provisioned_shape: {tool, tool_version, cpg, graph: {methods, type_declarations, files}, query_set, queries: [{id, bound, returned, bound_reached, elapsed_ms, callee_prefixes[]}], findings: [{query_id, severity, message, callee, class, method, file, line}]}

differences.documented: findings[].rule_id, one of five joern. prefixed literals
differences.consequence: Every rule_id below is a joern. prefixed identifier read from the first candidate of RULE_ID_FIELDS = ('rule_id', 'query_id'), so rule_id_from_rule_id counts 9 -- one per finding walked, including all six rejected ones, whose identifiers resolve at step 2 before their coordinate is examined -- and rule_id_from_query_id counts 0.

differences.documented: findings[].class_file, a class-file path such as org/apache/spark/deploy/master/Master.class
differences.observed_here: findings[].class_file on eight of the nine records and absent from the ninth (findings[2]); no class member is present on any record
differences.consequence: coordinate_from_class_file counts 8 and coordinate_from_class counts 0. The count is 8 rather than 9 because the provenance counter is bumped only where a candidate member was actually present in the record: normalize.adapters.joern._read_first tests presence rather than truthiness, so a class_file of null, '' or '   ' still counts as read while an absent member does not. The runner metadata names class as record_path_field, so the adapter tries it first and falls through to class_file, which is why a document in either shape resolves -- and why a record carrying neither member reaches the path step with read.field None and no coordinate_field identity key.

differences.observed_here: no severity member at all -- the literal string severity does not occur anywhere in the fixture
differences.consequence: Every surviving row carries severity_native null and severity_norm Info on the no_vocabulary basis, so severity_absent counts 3 and severity_from_record_label counts 0. This is the half of AAP 0.5.4's joern severity clause the positive fixture cannot show, since all six of this provisioning's baked queries declare HIGH or MEDIUM.
differences.why_this_is_the_contract: AAP 0.5.4 places joern under 'No vocabulary at all (gitleaks; joern unless a query defines one) -- severity_native absent, severity_norm Info, the absence stated rather than a level assumed'. Here no query defines one, so the absence is stated. Info is never written by the adapter directly: severity.py owns the vocabulary, the precedence and the bands, so this file cannot disagree with severity-map.md.

differences.documented: findings[].path, the collector's own already-root-relative answer, and findings[].path_resolution, its explanation of how it got there
differences.observed_here: both present on every record; path is null on all six defective records and root-relative on the three sound ones
differences.consequence: The null path on every defective record is load-bearing rather than incidental. For five of the six the adapter reaches its collector fallback after paths.resolve_bytecode_class returned a rejection, and for the sixth it reaches the same fallback from the sentinel branch; in both cases a usable root-relative collector path would have produced a row on that path marked uncorroborated, and the rejection would not exist. Because path is null throughout, collector_path_refused counts 0 and every rejection stands. The three sound records each carry a collector path identical to this run's own unique resolution, so collector_path_corroborated counts 3 while collector_path_disagreed counts 0. collector_explanation_present counts 9, because every record carries a path_resolution and the counter is taken before the path step decides the record's outcome.

differences.documented: flat cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size and declaration_index_size
differences.observed_here: all four present; no nested graph object
differences.consequence: envelope_graph_methods, envelope_graph_type_declarations, envelope_collector_source_index_size and envelope_collector_declaration_index_size all carry figures, while envelope_graph_files stays 0 because the nested object that would supply it is absent. The per-query tally is spelled count here rather than returned, and neither is summed into any published figure.

count_unit.per_query_tally_member: queries[].count in this shape; queries[].returned in the provisioned shape
count_unit.which_one_is_the_raw_count: len(findings) = 9. The sum of the per-query tallies is 669 -- 55 + 178 + 412 + 23 + 1 -- and is not the raw count and is not published as one.
count_unit.why_they_differ: The fixture carries 9 findings beside a queries[] array whose counts describe a whole scan. The two numbers therefore differ by construction, which is what makes the reconciliation assertion non-vacuous: an implementation that counted the per-query tallies instead of the findings would produce 669 against 3 rows and 6 rejections and fail loudly rather than agree silently.
count_unit.no_query_to_finding_link: No rule_id is ever taken from a queries[].id. The documented queries[] carries only {id, count} and records no link between a query and a finding, so a match there would be inference; each finding names its own query through its own rule_id member.
count_unit.authority: AAP 0.5.4 makes findings[] the reconciliation unit, and normalize.reconcile.count_records walks that same unit without building rows. The adapter deliberately publishes no count of the findings it walked, so the left-hand side of the identity cannot be taken from the traversal that builds the right-hand side. Measured on this fixture, it returns 9.
count_unit.a_defective_record_still_counts: Each of the six defective records is one element of findings[] and is counted as one raw record, exactly like a sound one. The independent traversal takes the length of the array and inspects no member, so a record's defect cannot change the left-hand side of the identity -- which is the property that makes 9 == 3 + 6 an assertion about the adapter rather than about the counter.

resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the joern entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.why_no_filesystem_base_exists: The runner queries a graph the frontend built over staged JARs rather than over the source tree, so a reported file member is by construction the frontend's extraction path for a .class member and can never be a path in the Spark tree. The metadata therefore records a null base value rather than inventing a plausible one, and the class coordinate is the only resolvable one. Because has_explicit_base is false, no metadata-backed fallback is available to this tool at all: a coordinate that resolves to nothing is rejected rather than anchored on a guessed base.
resolution_context.resolution_procedure: The class coordinate is reduced by joern_collect.class_key to <package path>/<outer type name>, truncating the basename at its first $ so a companion object, an anonymous class and a nested class all collapse to the outer type. That key is then looked up in a source index over src/main and src/test under the pinned root, across two key schemes: by_filename on <package dir>/<file base name>, and by_decl on <package dir>/<declared type name>. The union of candidates must be exactly one distinct path. This fixture's six defective records never reach the reduction at all: the guard for an absent identifier precedes it, which is why none of them can produce a class_key identity key and why none of them is malformed_record.
resolution_context.gap_1_closed: The index spans src/main and src/test rather than src/main alone. Every -tests artifact the build emitted is in the graph input, so a finding can legitimately name bytecode compiled from a test tree, and such a resolution is retained with in_scope false rather than dropped. No record in this fixture resolves into a test tree, so rows_from_src_test is 0 here.
resolution_context.gap_2_closed: A resolution is taken only where the union of candidates is exactly one distinct path. Two or more is ambiguous_source_resolution with every competing candidate named, never a first-wins pick. Closing gap 1 increases ambiguity, which is why closing gap 2 is mandatory rather than optional.
resolution_context.declaration_scheme_is_not_optional: One of the three surviving rows resolves on the declaration scheme alone: no file is named ProcessBuilderLike.scala, and DriverRunner.scala is the file that declares the type. A filename-only index would lose that row silently, and a silently lost row is indistinguishable from a class with nothing to report.
resolution_context.collector_path_precedence: Fixed by the adapter and exercised on every record here. This run's own unique class-to-source resolution governs; an ambiguous key is never overridden by the collector's answer; where this run resolves nothing and the collector did supply a root-relative path, that path is emitted as-is and marked uncorroborated; and where both resolve and differ, this run's answer is kept and the disagreement recorded. The three sound records take the first branch with the collector agreeing. All six defective records reach the third branch with the collector supplying null -- five of them after paths.resolve_bytecode_class rejected the identifier, and the sentinel record from the adapter's own sentinel branch -- so every rejection stands.
resolution_context.root_dependence: These rows depend on a live tree: the class-to-source resolution reads the pinned checkout at $SPARK_SRC. Every emitted path is expressed relative to that root and none is absolute, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file. The index figures under counters are the measurement over the pinned tree, and they reproduce the figures the adapter's own docstring records.
resolution_context.severity_source: No record states a severity, and this shape has no rule object to fall back on, so every row takes severity.py's no-vocabulary path: severity_native null, severity_norm Info, basis no_vocabulary. The absence is stated rather than a level assumed.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry. The absence is explicitly not a rejection: the unformable_package_coordinate class covers a dependency-oriented record, and this shape is not one.
resolution_context.what_this_fixture_adds_to_the_procedure: The absent-coordinate guard, which sits before the reduction and before the index lookup. paths.resolve_bytecode_class rejects an identifier that is None or that strips to nothing, with a fixed detail and before class_key is ever called; and normalize.adapters.joern intercepts the collector's '<unknown>' sentinel before that function is called at all. Neither route consults the source index, so neither can be affected by what the pinned tree contains -- which is why the artifact-determined counters below are the same whatever tree the test runs against, and why the five root-dependent index figures are the only values here that depend on a live checkout.

rejection_boundary.statement: A coordinate that is absent is a rejection under absent_path. A coordinate that is present and resolves to nothing is a rejection under unresolvable_path. A coordinate that resolves somewhere unwanted is a kept row with in_scope false. All six of this fixture's defective records fall in the first case: there is no coordinate to resolve, so the index is never consulted and the class name records that fact rather than a lookup that failed.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: path is one of only two never-absent fields in the twelve-field schema, the other being severity_norm: emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS carries path, and emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS is exactly severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate. A record with no resolvable path therefore has no valid row representation at all, so counting it under a named class is the only outcome that neither drops the record nor invents a coordinate for it.
rejection_boundary.why_absent_is_not_unresolvable: The two classes answer different questions and a reader of tool-status.md acts differently on each. unresolvable_path says the artifact named a class and this run's index over src/main and src/test held no source for it -- which for this tool is the ordinary outcome for a shaded third-party class, and which invites the question whether the index is complete. absent_path says the artifact named no class at all -- which is a property of the collector's output, not of the index, and invites the question why the collector emitted a finding it could not attribute. Collapsing the two would put 585 real index misses and a handful of unattributed findings under one name and make neither question answerable. The code keeps them apart structurally: the absent guard in paths.resolve_bytecode_class returns before class_key is called, so no key and no candidate set exists for an absent coordinate, and the sentinel branch in the adapter returns before resolve_bytecode_class is called at all.
rejection_boundary.why_absent_is_not_malformed: malformed_record covers a record whose shape is not what the artifact contract says -- a finding that is not an object, a message that is not a string, a class identifier that is not a string. A class_file of null, '' or '   ' is not a wrong type: null is the JSON spelling of an absent value, and an empty or whitespace-only string is a string. The guard order in paths.resolve_bytecode_class makes this explicit: the absent test runs first and catches None and any string that strips to nothing, and only then does the non-string test catch a wrong type. So a class_file of null is absent_path and a class_file of 42 would be malformed_record, and reject-joern-malformed-record.json owns the second.

not_a_rejection.case: a resolution into a src/test tree, from a -tests artifact in the graph input
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope and rows_from_src_test
not_a_rejection.evidence: AAP 0.5.4 requires a test-JAR finding kept out of scope rather than dropped, and AAP 0.9.3 repeats it among the recorded-not-halting conditions. The literal src/test exclusion lives in paths.in_scope and removes the path from scope, never from the dataset.

not_a_rejection.case: a resolution outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: A class in a module the allowlist does not name resolves to a real file and is kept. Out of scope means kept and marked.

not_a_rejection.case: a collector-supplied path naming an archive member or a location above the root
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted in non_filesystem_paths
not_a_rejection.evidence: Serialized as <container-relative-to-root>!<member> with ! the single separator, and with ../ segments preserved rather than normalized. The kind is read off the serialized form by paths.path_kind_for, so the discrimination is made on the string that actually reaches the dataset.

rejection_boundary.no_guessed_path: Each of the six rejected records is rejected and counted, never given a path. Nothing in this file supplies a coordinate for any of them, not even a plausible one -- and for five of the six there is no coordinate in the artifact from which a plausible one could be derived. The method_full_name each carries would make an inviting substitute, since a dotted method signature does contain a type name; the adapter does not use it, and the identity below carries it as diagnosable context rather than as a coordinate.
rejection_boundary.why_the_method_signature_is_not_a_fallba: Every defective record here names its enclosing method, and four of the six name a method on a type whose source is in the pinned tree -- Utils$, JavaDeserializationStream, CommandUtils$, SparkEnv$, Master. A resolver that fell back to the method signature would therefore turn all six of these rejections into rows, and would look like an improvement. It is not one: the metadata records the class member as record_path_field, so the coordinate the collector is contracted to supply is the class, and deriving one from a method signature would be inference of exactly the kind AAP 0.5.4 forbids -- 'a record that cannot be attributed with certainty is rejected and the rejection recorded as a class with its count, never inferred into a field'. The signature is carried into the rejection identity so the record can be found again, and reaches no dataset field.

why_this_rejection_path_is_native.statement: An absent coordinate is a thing a collector over a bytecode graph produces in the ordinary course, not an anomaly staged for a test. Two of the six shapes below are documented behaviours of the collector contract itself, and the other four are the spellings an absence takes in JSON.

categories.category: a method with no enclosing type declaration
categories.explanation: harness/lib/joern-scan.sc writes the string '<unknown>' where a matched method has no enclosing TypeDecl in the graph -- a synthetic lambda body, a bridge, a frontend-generated accessor. joern_collect exposes that literal as COLLECTOR_UNKNOWN_CLASS precisely so a consumer treats it as a stated absence rather than as a class name, and the adapter classifies it as an absent coordinate with the sentinel named in the detail.
categories.this_fixture: findings[6] is this category, and it is the one record of the six that takes the sentinel route through the adapter rather than the guard in paths.resolve_bytecode_class. unknown_class_sentinel_records counts 1.

categories.category: a finding the collector could attribute to no class
categories.explanation: A collector that emits a finding whose coordinate it could not determine writes the member as null, as an empty string, or omits it. All three are the same statement -- no class -- expressed three ways, and a consumer that handled one and not the others would reject some and silently drop or misclassify the rest.
categories.this_fixture: findings[1] carries class_file null, findings[2] omits the member entirely, findings[3] carries the empty string, findings[4] carries three spaces and findings[5] carries a tab and a newline. Five spellings, one class, and one shared detail string.

categories.category: a class member present and resolving to nothing
categories.explanation: The neighbouring condition, and deliberately not this fixture's: a shaded or otherwise third-party class whose source is in another project's repository. It is unresolvable_path, and over the real artifact it is five of every six findings.
categories.this_fixture: Excluded by construction. The sibling fixture's shaded MessageDigestHashFunction record was dropped when this fixture was derived from it, so no record here can produce that class and the six rejections are one class rather than two.

why_this_rejection_path_is_native.will_be_exercised_by_the_real_artifact: Stated precisely rather than overclaimed. Over harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json's 692 findings the adapter produces 107 rows and 585 rejections, and every one of the 585 is under unresolvable_path -- absent_path occurs zero times, because this provisioning's collector shape names a class on every finding it wrote and its run produced no '<unknown>' method. That is what makes a committed fixture necessary rather than optional: the condition is reachable from the artifact contract, the collector script writes the sentinel that reaches it, and no production artifact happens to exercise it. AAP 0.9.4 requires a negative fixture for every rejection condition an exercised adapter can produce 'whether or not this run's own artifacts contained that case', and this is that case.
why_this_rejection_path_is_native.why_it_must_be_counted_with_its_own_clas: Three consequences, each sufficient on its own. A record with no coordinate has no valid row representation, so the alternatives are to drop it or to invent a coordinate, and both are invisible downstream. Counting it under unresolvable_path instead would make the tool's largest rejection class -- 585 index misses over the real artifact -- unable to distinguish a missing index entry from a missing coordinate, which is the difference between a question about this pipeline and a question about the collector. And the sentinel route in particular carries the collector's own account of why it could not attribute the method; that account survives only in the rejection detail, and a rejection folded into another class loses the part of the detail that named it.
why_this_rejection_path_is_native.no_judgement: None of this characterises any finding. Whether a reflective class load or a deserialization site matters is not this pipeline's question, and nothing here rules on it. The six records are rejected for having no coordinate, which is a statement about the record and not about the code it names.

rejection_pair.this_half: absent -- nothing to look up. No class coordinate exists on the record, so no key is built, no candidate set is computed and the index is never consulted. The class is paths.REJECT_ABSENT_PATH.
rejection_pair.sibling_half: unresolvable -- looked up and nothing found. A class coordinate exists, class_key reduces it, and the union of candidates over src/main and src/test is empty. The class is paths.REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH.
rejection_pair.why_each_needs_its_own_diagnosis: Both are rejections and both leave the record out of the dataset, so a test that only counted rejections could not tell them apart -- which is why the class name is what carries the assertion. They differ in four ways that matter. The class differs, so tool-status.md attributes them to different conditions. The detail differs: this one says no coordinate remains to resolve, while the sibling's names the simple name, the package searched and both source trees. The identity differs: the sibling's carries class and class_key, because the reduction ran; five of these carry class with a null or blank value and no class_key at all, because the guard returned before the reduction, and the sixth carries neither. And the code path differs, which is the sharpest of the four: the sibling's rejection comes from the index lookup returning an empty candidate set, so it depends on what the pinned tree contains; these six are decided before any tree is read, so they are the same under any checkout.
rejection_pair.derived_from_the_sibling: This fixture is the sibling with its defective record replaced by six of its own and its three sound records kept, so the two are directly comparable: the same envelope, the same query set, the same three rows, the same three row derivations. Everything that differs between the two expected files is therefore attributable to the condition rather than to the fixture, which is what makes the pair a controlled comparison instead of two unrelated documents.
rejection_pair.opposite_reasons_note: Nothing to look up and looked up and nothing found are different failures of different requirements -- that a record name a coordinate at all, and that a named coordinate resolve uniquely -- so covering one does not cover the other, and neither fixture makes the other redundant.

the_two_classification_routes.note: absent_path is one class produced by two distinct code paths, and which path a record takes decides its detail string and its identity key set. Both are exercised here, and a fixture covering only one would leave the other's spelling unasserted.

route_a.name: the absent-identifier guard in normalize.paths.resolve_bytecode_class
route_a.reached_when: the adapter read a coordinate value that is None or a string that strips to nothing, or read no coordinate member at all, and the value is not the collector's sentinel
route_a.mechanism: normalize.adapters.joern._resolve_class_coordinate hands the read value to paths.resolve_bytecode_class, whose first act is to seed the identity key class with the identifier as given and whose first guard rejects None and any string that strips to nothing. class_key is never called, so no class_key key is added and no candidate set is computed.
route_a.detail: the finding carries no class identifier, and the runner metadata records the file field as the one to ignore, so no coordinate remains to resolve; collector path_resolution: unresolved-bytecode-only
route_a.detail_is_fixed: The detail interpolates nothing. It is the same string for a null, an empty, a whitespace-only and an omitted coordinate, which is correct: the four are one condition spelled four ways and a reader acts identically on all four. Which spelling a record carried is recoverable from the identity, where class holds the value as given.
route_a.collector_explanation_not_appended: The absent-identifier guard is the one branch of resolve_bytecode_class that does not pass its detail through _with_collector_explanation, so the record's path_resolution of 'unresolved-bytecode-only' does not appear in these five details. route_a.identity_keys: finding_index, then each present context member, then rule_id, then coordinate_field where a coordinate member was present, then class -- and never class_key, because the reduction did not run

route_b.name: the sentinel branch in normalize.adapters.joern._resolve_class_coordinate
route_b.reached_when: the coordinate value strips to joern_collect.COLLECTOR_UNKNOWN_CLASS, the literal '<unknown>'
route_b.mechanism: The adapter intercepts the sentinel before paths.resolve_bytecode_class is called at all, tries the collector's own path member, and where that supplies nothing builds the rejection itself -- interpolating the coordinate member it read and the metadata's record_path_field_to_ignore, and appending the collector's explanation through its own _with_explanation.
route_b.detail: the finding's class_file is the collector's '<unknown>' sentinel, written where a method has no enclosing type declaration, so it names no class to resolve; the metadata records file as the field to ignore, so no coordinate remains; collector path_resolution: unresolved-bytecode-only
route_b.detail_is_interpolated: Three values come from outside the string: the coordinate member read (class_file), the metadata's record_path_field_to_ignore (file), and the record's own path_resolution (unresolved-bytecode-only). So the detail names the sentinel, names the member that carried it, and retains the collector's own account -- which is the evidence that separates 'the collector could not attribute this method' from 'this pipeline read the wrong member'.
route_b.why_it_must_not_be_an_index_lookup: Keying the source index on the literal '<unknown>' would turn a stated absence into an ordinary lookup miss: the key would reduce to '<unknown>' with zero candidates and the record would be rejected under unresolvable_path with a detail claiming no source file is named '<unknown>' in the package ''. The class would be wrong, the detail would be nonsense, and the collector's own explanation of the absence would be the only surviving evidence that anything had gone wrong. The interception is what prevents that.
route_b.identity_keys: finding_index, then each present context member, then rule_id, then coordinate_field -- and neither class nor class_key, because resolve_bytecode_class was never called and nothing seeded them

the_six_defective_shapes.coverage_claim: These six are every way a coordinate can be absent from a record this adapter accepts as well-formed. A value of the wrong type is malformed_record and belongs to reject-joern-malformed-record.json; a value that is present, non-blank and not the sentinel reaches the index and is either a row, ambiguous_source_resolution or unresolvable_path, and those three have their own fixtures. the_six_defective_shapes.the_class_member_is_absent_throughout: No record in this fixture carries a class member, only class_file, because the fixture is in the documented shape. The adapter reads class first and falls through, so the coordinate provenance is class_file on all eight records that carry a coordinate member. A provisioned-shape record with an absent class member and no class_file would take the same route as findings[2] here.

collector_explanation_retention.statement: The collector's path_resolution reaches the rejection detail on both routes. Every branch that cannot map a bytecode coordinate composes the collector's own account into the detail it records, so the six details all end with '; collector path_resolution: unresolved-bytecode-only'.
collector_explanation_retention.both_routes_retain_it: Route B is built by normalize.adapters.joern's own sentinel branch and route A by paths.resolve_bytecode_class's absent-identifier branch; both pass their detail through paths._with_collector_explanation, which appends '; collector path_resolution: <value>' where the record carries one. An earlier form of this pipeline composed it on the malformed, ambiguous and unresolvable branches only, so the absent-identifier branch returned its fixed detail directly and rejections 0 to 4 carried no suffix. That gap is closed: retention is uniform across the branches.
collector_explanation_retention.why_retention_is_required: The collector's explanation is evidence about the collector, and a rejection is the only place it can be recorded -- AAP 0.5.4 keeps it in the rejection record and out of every dataset field. Retaining it on one branch and not another made two records of one condition differ in what they preserved, and a reader could not tell whether the silent branch had no explanation to record or had dropped one.
collector_explanation_retention.what_is_not_lost: The explanation is also a member of the record, and the rejection identity carries finding_index, so path_resolution stays recoverable from the artifact for every one of the six independently of the detail string.
collector_explanation_retention.confinement: Retention is confined to the rejection: no row is produced for any of the six, and no dataset field on any row this fixture does produce carries the explanation. That is the half the tests assert on every route regardless of which branch composed the detail.

counts.two_thirds_rejected: This is the only Joern fixture in which rejections outnumber rows, which is deliberate: six shapes need six records, and the three sound neighbours are there to prove the adapter carries on rather than to balance the arithmetic.
